title: Nestree Residence: big family layouts beside Bangsar South.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #460 | NESTREE RESIDENCE, PANTAI SENTRAL PARK
excerpt: A newly completed condo in Pantai Sentral Park, next to Bangsar South. Sean tours an owner's four-bedroom corner unit and finds a design-led deck, with a few flaws.
takeaways: A two-level deck with several pools, a badminton hall, a glass gym and fully furnished activity rooms.
Bought at about RM600 psf; a 1,275 sq ft four-bedroom now asks about RM900,000, or about RM3,500 a month unfurnished.
Dark, echoing lift lobbies, hidden corners and plenty of nearby supply are the concerns.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Nestree sits in Pantai Sentral Park, a township whose roads, drains and walkways were finished before the buildings. A loud water feature at the entrance masks traffic noise. The two-level deck has an infinity lap pool, jacuzzi, wading and kids' pools, a covered playground, an air-conditioned two-court badminton hall and a glass gym, with arts, reading, co-working and games rooms all furnished for use; the roof adds a function hall, sky lounges and karaoke rooms.

Sean tours an owner's Type C, the one corner unit on each floor: 1,275 sq ft with four bedrooms, three bathrooms, an L-shaped balcony, a dry kitchen and a large wet kitchen, and a helper's room with its own bathroom. Each floor has about 22 units across two lift cores. Buyers paid about RM600 to RM650 psf.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is next to Bangsar South, beside the NPE, which is getting a second deck. The NPE leads to Sunway, Kuchai Lama and Sungai Besi, while Old Klang Road, KL Eco City, Bangsar and KL Sentral are close by. Inside the township there is only a McDonald's drive-through for now. The unit looks over a sewage treatment plant by the highway, though Sean noticed no smell or noise.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: This unit type now asks about RM900,000 on the subsale market, and about RM3,500 a month to rent unfurnished. Based on projects nearby, Sean thinks a fully furnished unit could let for RM3,800 to RM4,200. The project has sold out, so only subsale units remain.

pros: The location, especially for anyone working in Bangsar South: the NPE, Old Klang Road, KL Eco City and KL Sentral are all close, with Bangsar South's offices and shops next door. Inside the township, though, there is only a McDonald's drive-through until neighbouring phases open in about four years.

The common areas: a water feature that masks the traffic, a polished lobby, two floors of facilities with several pools, orange-painted pathways and a full-glass gym. Most impressive, every room, from the arts room to the badminton hall, is furnished to be used rather than just labelled.
The corner layout: openings on two sides, every bedroom facing out, and a generous back of house with dry and wet kitchens, plus a helper's room or storeroom.
cons: The lift cores: set away from any facade and lit by yellow downlights, they feel dark and a little eerie, with an odd corridor that leads nowhere. Broken door stoppers make the fire doors slam and echo, and owners complained about lift speed and size.
The structural system: well built, with transfer slabs and neat car park finishes, but the lobby and facility deck are full of hidden corners, some of them unsafe.

Density: Residensi Alamanda, the project opposite and later phases of the township, plus River Park, 9 Seputeh and Old Klang Road nearby, give buyers plenty of choice at this price, so do more homework.

closing: Beyond Sean's expectations for own stay and investment alike, once the dark corridors and lifts are sorted out.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this August 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner invited Sean to view his unit at handover; resale prices and rents are asking figures Sean quoted.
